---
title: Branch
description: "A collection of records with the same fields, such as an account's transactions."
engine: markdown
---

`Branch` groups repeated records that have the same fields. In this
account-review example, each observation contains the transactions available
at one cutoff, and the task is to predict later disputes for those transactions.
The `trxns` branch keeps earlier events and the latest payment in one sequence,
with each timestamp, amount, and merchant together. This gives the model
context within an event and across the sequence.

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    trxns=rf.Branch(
        length=32,
        overflow="tail",
        booked_at=rf.DateParts(
            dateparts=["day_of_month", "day_of_week", "hour_of_day"],
        ),
        amount=rf.Number,
        merchant=rf.Category,
        disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
    ),
)
```

One account review observation, ordered oldest to latest:

```yaml
trxns:
  - booked_at: "2026-05-21T10:00:00"
    amount: 32.00
    merchant: Station Cafe
    disputed: false
  - booked_at: "2026-05-27T18:15:00"
    amount: 56.20
    merchant: North Market
    disputed: true
  - booked_at: "2026-05-28T14:30:00"
    amount: 84.50
    merchant: North Market
    disputed: false
```

`length=32` keeps at most 32 transactions. `overflow="tail"` keeps the most
recent ones, including the latest payment, when the application supplies this
order. A [preprocessor](../guides/preprocessing.qmd) owns sorting.
`mask=True` hides and predicts the dispute label for every transaction, and
prediction records omit it. [Prepare observations](../learn/prepare-observations.qmd)
defines the cutoff and label window these records follow.

## Binding and shape

The parent keyword supplies the collection name. With `query=None`,
`trxns` reads the same-named child collection, and its leaves read
keys within each transaction. Use a [query](../guides/query-paths.qmd) for
a different structural path and a preprocessor for sorting, filtering, or derived
values.

A child branch requires a list of objects, including when `length=1`. Only
the generated model root reads one object directly. Each child branch adds a
repeated axis. Its execution width follows the selected collections in each
batch; an explicit `length` caps retained items. Padding does not contribute to
attention or reduction, but it still has storage and processing costs.
[Prediction output](../reference/prediction-output.qmd#repeated-coordinates) writes
every record collection as a variable Arrow list of sibling result structs,
without public cap padding. Structural nulls and empty collections are preserved.

A branch can own nested branches: purchases within transactions can each vary
in length while remaining attached to their parent transaction. Declare the
complete finite tree in the schema; collection lengths can then vary between
observations without changing its field definitions. See
[Nested context and account outcomes](../learn/nested-context-and-account-outcomes.qmd).

Definitions are reusable: binding clones them without changing the original.
Use `fields={"length": rf.Number}` for generated schemas or child names that
collide with configuration. Use [Set](set.qmd) for membership alone and
[Vector](vector.qmd) for one numeric vector.

## Automatic lengths and limits {#automatic-lengths-and-limits}

Omitting `length`, or setting `length=None`, retains every collection slot:

```python
history = rf.Branch(
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
)
```

Each batch uses the largest retained collection length, including null object
slots. Widths can grow or shrink between batches; all-empty collections have
width zero. Nested widths are resolved after any parent limit has selected its
records. Leaves beneath the same branch share its geometry, independently of
values, masking, or which target is supplied. This changes execution geometry,
without updating the schema, growing parameters, or replacing the optimizer.

Set a positive integer `length` for a hard limit. Only bounded branches accept
`overflow="head"`, `"tail"`, or `"error"`; omission or `None` selects `"head"`
when a limit exists. `Branch(overflow="tail", ...)` without a finite length is
an error. The generated root always remains a singleton with `length=1` and
internal `overflow="error"`.

Bounded branches also pad only to the largest retained length in each batch,
up to their cap. This internal execution width does not add padding to public
record collections.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Inference-time DoS/DDoS attack vector

With `length=None`, untrusted requests control nested collection sizes during
inference. Oversized collections can exhaust CPU/GPU memory or compute and deny
service to other users. Requests from multiple sources can amplify this into a
distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack.

Set finite branch lengths and enforce request-size limits before
[public serving](../guides/serving.qmd#bound-public-requests). A batch-size limit
alone does not bound nested collections. RelFlow logs one aggregate warning per
model generation for active unbounded branches; the warning enforces no limit.
No hidden cap is applied to `length=None`.
:::

## Random training windows {#random-training-windows}

Use a finite `length` with `overflow="random"` to vary the retained history
during training:

```python
history = rf.Branch(
    length=32,
    overflow="random",
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
)
```

When a collection exceeds the cap, training selects a contiguous window of
32 whole records, preserving their order. With 80 records, its starting
position is drawn uniformly from 0 through 48. Fields and nested children
remain attached to the same record; null items still count as collection
slots. Collections at or below the cap are unchanged.

| Loop | Retained records |
| --- | --- |
| Training | A randomly selected contiguous window. |
| Validation, test, prediction | The tail, deterministically. |

The source or preprocessor must supply more than 32 eligible records for
this example to vary. If an upstream query has already kept only the latest
32, random overflow has no effect. Supply a larger, separately bounded
candidate pool while preserving the scoring cutoff and desired ordering.
The model's cap does not bound the cost of loading or preparing that pool.

Crops repeat for the same data seed, epoch, batch ordinal, branch address,
and parent position within a batch. Changing batching, worker assignment, or
row order can change them. A random window can omit the latest payment; keep
`overflow="tail"` when that payment must always be included. Uniform window
starts also do not give every item the same inclusion probability.

## Options

These are the direct `rf.Branch` defaults. A
[size preset](../concepts/model-tree.qmd#choose-a-size) such as
`Model.xs` fills omitted branch settings; explicit node settings take precedence.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | `None` | Named child mapping, combinable with keyword children; names must be unique. |
| `query` | `None` | Optional node-relative structural path. |
| `length` | `None` | Automatic batch width; a positive integer caps retained items per parent coordinate. |
| `overflow` | `None` | Unbounded branches require `None`. With finite `length`, omission becomes `"head"`; choose `"head"`, `"tail"`, or `"error"`. The [`"random"` policy](#random-training-windows) samples training windows and keeps the tail for evaluation. Order comes from the processed source. |
| `attention` | `"mha"` | Encoder mode; see below. |
| `n_layers` | `1` | Positive sequence-encoder depth. |
| `n_heads` | `4` | Positive, even encoder head count and fallback for Attention reduction. Active attention requires heads to divide `d_model` with at least two dimensions per head. |
| `ffnx` | `8` | Positive integer feed-forward multiplier for this branch's encoders and learned reduction. See [model-tree configuration](../concepts/model-tree.qmd#configure-the-context). |
| `reduction` | `rf.Attention()` | What encoded memory reaches the parent. |
| `dropout` | `None` | Optional encoder dropout in `[0, 1)` and reduction fallback. |
| `mask` | `False` | Visibility and reconstruction policy applied atomically to active descendants. |
| `embed` | `False` | Export this branch's contextual embedding. |
| `description` | `None` | Human-readable notes. |

Branch settings are local. Model settings configure the generated singleton
root; they do not replace every child branch's defaults.

## Attention and reduction {#reduce-branch-memory}

An attention-enabled branch first mixes direct sibling leaves and summaries
from reduced child branches at each aligned record coordinate, when there is
more than one participating token. Its `n_layers` sequence stack
then mixes child slots across the branch. Finally, reduction chooses the
representations routed to its parent.

| Encoder mode | Key/value heads |
| --- | --- |
| `"mha"` | One per query head. |
| `"gqa"` | One per pair of query heads. |
| `"mqa"` | One shared by every query head. |
| `None` | No coordinate or sequence attention; reduction still runs. |

Sharing key/value heads changes model capacity as well as cost.

| Reduction | Parent receives | Tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rf.Attention(n_outputs=1)` | A fixed number of learned summaries. | Bounded memory; outputs do not guarantee item identity. |
| `rf.Mean()` | One average of present encoded vectors plus a learned count lane. | Cheap; multiplicity survives through the count lane, while order and individual values are not directly preserved. |
| `None` | Every encoded child slot with its presence state. | Keeps token correspondence available; increases parent sequence cost. |

`Attention` has `n_outputs=1`, `n_layers=1`, `n_heads=None`, `dropout=None`,
and `position=True`. Counts are positive. Omitted heads and dropout inherit
from the branch; explicit values override them. `position` controls rotary
position in the reducer only. `Mean` has no tuning options. These configurations
are frozen and share settings, not learned weights, when reused.

`attention=None` and `reduction=None` skip different operations. Use both for
pure pass-through. Turning off reducer position alone does not remove position
information from earlier encoder attention.

Choose reduction from the evidence the parent needs. A mean is not a raw-field
sum, and more learned summaries do not perform a join. Capacity must survive
later reductions too. `model.schema.branch_outputs` reports each branch's
static routed width, or `None` when pass-through width depends on the batch.

The [nested cardinality evidence](../evidence/structure/attention-preserves-nested-cardinality.html)
tests whether session summaries preserve enough information for their parent.
The [Mean control](../evidence/structure/mean-keeps-cardinality.html) shows that
Mean's count lane keeps the multiplicity a plain average would lose.

## Masks and output

`disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True)` keeps the answer out of the inputs and
produces a dispute prediction for every transaction. The predictions retain
their transaction positions; the branch groups those results and has no typed
prediction value of its own.

`embed=True` exports branch context at its address. See
[Reusable representations](../learn/reusable-representations.qmd) for output roles and
[Model tree](../concepts/model-tree.qmd) for the route through nested contexts.
